title: When love ends
hookLine: a breakup, a half-typed message, and an old line on hatred and love
tomorrow: an old list of how parents care for a child has no hugs in it. why?

cards: Late at night, a thumb hovers over a name. Block, or mute, or post the sad song everyone will understand.

The breakup was weeks ago, and the group chat has opinions: never text back, never say their name, make sure they know what they lost. There's a message half-typed in the box, and it isn't kind. Here's the strange part.
The person typing it once wished this other person well every single day, without trying. Where did that wish go? Did it have to end with everything else?

teach.h: HE ABUSED ME, HE ROBBED ME.
teach.b: Near its start, the Dhammapada has that exact message in someone's head: he abused me, he beat me, he robbed me. In those who keep turning thoughts like that over, the verse says, hatred never stops.
Then a line Max Müller translated plainly: "For hatred does not cease by hatred at any time: hatred ceases by love, this is an old rule." Notice what it doesn't say.
It doesn't say stay together, or stay friends, or pretend it didn't hurt. An ending can be right; sometimes leaving is the kindest thing two people do. What the verse watches is the wish underneath.
Later, the teacher Buddhaghosa gave metta, loving-kindness, two enemies. The far enemy is ill will, easy to spot.

teach.h: THE NEAR ENEMY LOOKS LIKE LOVE.
teach.b: The near enemy is greed, wanting, which can look exactly like love. A breakup is when you find out which one was there.
If the wish for their good disappears the moment they stop being yours, it may have been wanting all along. If it can survive at a distance, that was metta.
And if it's buried under hurt right now, it can take a while to come back. That's allowed. So kind at the end isn't staying.
It's leaving without sending the cruel message.
You can mute them, keep your distance, grieve hard, and still not wish them harm.
The relationship ends. The wish for their good doesn't have to.

how: Buddhists practice metta, wishing beings well, at home and in temples; some teachers suggest bringing a former partner or a difficult person into that practice only once it feels safe.

o: a sign that the bond was never really real
an ending where the wish for their good can stay
the point where you must stop caring at all

games.q: the wish under the ending — tap the pairs.

s: being kind after a breakup means staying friends
the verse asks you to drop hatred; it doesn't ask you to stay close.
Buddhaghosa named greed as the near enemy of metta
it can look exactly like love; an ending shows which one was there.
the Dhammapada says hatred ends once you get even
it says the opposite: hatred does not cease by hatred.

games.q: your ex is seated at the next table at your cousin's wedding. what does kind at the end look like here?
o: go over and reconnect; real metta means getting close again.
be polite, keep your distance, and quietly wish them well.
leave early so you never have to deal with them at all.
games.why: the verse asks for no hatred, not for closeness. distance is allowed; ill will is what the teaching sets down.

practice: Bring to mind someone from your past: a former partner, or a friend you drifted from. Choose someone it feels safe to think about, and skip anyone who harmed you, for now.
From wherever you are, wish them one plain thing: may you be well. You don't have to want them back to mean it.

wordCard.voice: When love ends: the moment metta gets tested. The bond can stop, and the wish for someone's good can stay.

orig.note: Pali: loving-kindness, the wish that beings be well and happy.

carryVoice: Hold on to this: kind at the end, even from far away. Seven of eleven on family.

sources.q: For hatred does not cease by hatred at any time: hatred ceases by love, this is an old rule.

sources.ref: Dhammapada 3-4 (he abused me, he beat me, he robbed me; in those who harbor such thoughts hatred will never cease)
Visuddhimagga IX (the near enemy of loving-kindness is greed; the far enemy is ill will)
